Jesus goes on to warn that if a person is set free from an evil spirit but does not let the Holy Spirit dwell in him, that emptiness makes him even more open to attack by evil spirits again, and even worse than before. So we must let God's Spirit dwell in our hearts and keep spiritually alert, so that we do not fall into greater temptation and danger.

Through this passage God reminds us that in spiritual warfare it is only by depending on God's strength that we can overcome and guard our hearts. We need to keep seeking intimacy with God and let the Holy Spirit rule our lives, so that we can stand firm against temptation and challenge and avoid greater danger.
q: In your life, have you let the Holy Spirit dwell in and govern every corner of your heart? When you face spiritual challenges, how do you depend on God's strength to overcome?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for protecting us in spiritual warfare. Fill our lives with the Holy Spirit, so that we are strong in the face of temptation and keep trusting in your strength. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: It came to pass, as he said these things, a certain woman out of the multitude lifted up her voice, and said to him, “Blessed is the womb that bore you, and the breasts which nursed you!”
b: In this passage, while Jesus is teaching the crowd, a woman calls out loudly in praise of Jesus' mother, saying she is blessed. Her words reflect the esteem that society of that day had for mothers, especially mothers of great sons. Jesus' response, however, is unexpected: he says that those who are truly blessed are the ones who hear the word of God and keep it.

Jesus' answer shifts the focus from the blessing of family ties and social standing to spiritual blessing. Jesus stresses that the truly blessed are those who hear God's word and do it. This reminds us that spiritual blessing far surpasses every worldly blessing, because it rests on our relationship with God and obedience to his will.

Through this passage God tells us that true blessing comes from hearing and obeying his word. This is what Jesus values, and it is what he hopes for each of us. When we let God's word guide our lives and are willing to obey his leading, we can experience true blessing, a blessing that goes beyond all outward circumstances and conditions.
q: Today, are you faithfully obeying God's word in your life? How can you obey his will more deeply and experience true blessing through it?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for giving us your word as the guide for our lives. Help us not only to listen to your word but to faithfully obey it in life. May we receive true blessing because we obey your will. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: When the multitudes were gathering together to him, he began to say, “This is an evil generation. It seeks after a sign. No sign will be given to it but the sign of Jonah, the prophet.
For even as Jonah became a sign to the Ninevites, so the Son of Man will also be to this generation.

The Queen of the South will rise up in the judgment with the men of this generation, and will condemn them: for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and behold, one greater than Solomon is here.
The men of Nineveh will stand up in the judgment with this generation, and will condemn it: for they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and behold, one greater than Jonah is here.
b: In this passage Jesus responds to the crowd's demand and rebukes them as an evil generation, because they keep asking to see a sign but are unwilling to believe. Jesus says that no sign will be given to this generation except the sign of Jonah. He mentions that the people of Nineveh repented at Jonah's preaching, yet now there is one greater than Jonah, Jesus himself, and still this generation refuses to repent.

Jesus' words remind us that faith should not be built on the pursuit of signs, but on trusting and obeying God's word. The sign of Jonah was a call to the people of Nineveh to repent and turn to God. In the same way, Jesus came into the world to save people and lead them to repentance, but this generation often stubbornly refuses to accept him.

Through this passage God tells us that he wants us to have a heart willing to repent and obey, not one that keeps demanding to see miracles. True faith lies in listening to God's word, receiving it, and being willing to let it change our lives. When we are willing to answer God's call, his grace will be shown in our lives.
q: In your life, do you rely too much on miracles or outward evidence to support your faith? Today, how can you rely more on God's word and let it guide your actions?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for showing us your love and salvation through Jesus Christ. Help us to stop chasing signs and instead listen to and obey your word, so that our lives are changed and renewed under your guidance. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: “No one, when he has lit a lamp, puts it in a cellar or under a basket, but on a stand, that those who come in may see the light.
The lamp of the body is the eye. Therefore when your eye is good, your whole body is also full of light; but when it is evil, your body also is full of darkness.
Therefore see whether the light that is in you isn’t darkness.
If therefore your whole body is full of light, having no part dark, it will be wholly full of light, as when the lamp with its bright shining gives you light.”
b: In this passage Jesus uses the picture of a lamp to teach his disciples how to live the spiritual life. He points out that no one lights a lamp and hides it, but puts it on a stand so that everyone can see the light. In the same way, our eye is the lamp of our body, and whether it is clear or dark directly affects our spiritual condition. Jesus calls us to examine the light within us, to make sure our whole body is full of light and not darkness.

This passage reminds us that spiritual health and purity are vital to our lives. Our eye represents our heart; when our heart is fixed on God's light, our whole life is filled with light. But if our heart is clouded by sin or the temptations of the world, we fall into spiritual darkness. Jesus teaches us to keep examining ourselves, to make sure our hearts stay in God's light, so that our lives can be a witness to the world.

Through this passage God tells us that spiritual light comes from focusing on God and obeying his word. We should let God's light shine in our hearts, so that our lives reflect his glory. When our hearts are aligned with God, we can be his lighthouse in this dark world, guiding more people into his light.
q: Today, have you let God's light shine into every corner of your heart? How can your life better reflect God's light and be a witness to the world?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for letting your light shine into our lives. Help us to keep examining our hearts and to stay in your light, and make our lives a witness to your glory. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: Now as he spoke, a certain Pharisee asked him to dine with him. He went in, and sat at the table.
When the Pharisee saw it, he marveled that he had not first washed himself before dinner.
The Lord said to him, “Now you Pharisees cleanse the outside of the cup and of the platter, but your inward part is full of extortion and wickedness.
You foolish ones, didn’t he who made the outside make the inside also?
But give for gifts to the needy those things which are within, and behold, all things will be clean to you.
But woe to you Pharisees! For you tithe mint and rue and every herb, but you bypass justice and God’s love. You ought to have done these, and not to have left the other undone.
Woe to you Pharisees! For you love the best seats in the synagogues, and the greetings in the marketplaces.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like hidden graves, and the men who walk over them don’t know it.”
b: In this passage Jesus accepts a Pharisee's invitation to a meal, but the Pharisee is astonished that Jesus did not wash his hands before eating according to Jewish tradition. Jesus takes the opportunity to sharply rebuke the Pharisees' hypocrisy, pointing out that they care only about outward ritual and surface cleanness, while neglecting justice and the love of God within the heart.

Jesus stresses that true cleanness comes from within, not from outward ritual. The Pharisees focused on religious ceremony and overlooked what God values most: justice, mercy and love for God. This passage warns us not to become people who care only about outward religious form, but to value honesty of heart and true worship of God.

Through this passage God reminds us that what he values is the attitude of our hearts, not outward behavior. Our faith should be real and consistent inside and out, reflecting our love for God and our pursuit of his righteousness. When our hearts are aligned with God's will, our lives become a truly clean offering, acceptable to God.
q: In your life of faith, do you focus too much on outward ritual and neglect inner change? Today, how can you worship and follow God more truly, both in heart and in conduct?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for teaching us to value cleanness of heart. Help us not only to care about outward behavior but to pursue inner righteousness and love for you. May our faith be real and consistent inside and out, and pleasing to you. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: One of the lawyers answered him, “Teacher, in saying this you insult us also.”
He said, “Woe to you lawyers also! For you load men with burdens that are difficult to carry, and you yourselves won’t even lift one finger to help carry those burdens.
Woe to you! For you build the tombs of the prophets, and your fathers killed them.
So you testify and consent to the works of your fathers. For they killed them, and you build their tombs.
Therefore also the wisdom of God said, ‘I will send to them prophets and apostles; and some of them they will kill and persecute,
that the blood of all the prophets, which was shed from the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation;
from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zachariah, who perished between the altar and the sanctuary.’ Yes, I tell you, it will be required of this generation.
Woe to you lawyers! For you took away the key of knowledge. You didn’t enter in yourselves, and those who were entering in, you hindered.”
b: In this passage, after rebuking the Pharisees, Jesus turns his words to the lawyers, saying that they too are under woe, because they load people with burdens of the law that are hard to bear, while they themselves will not lift a finger to help. Their hypocrisy and false goodness make them a religious stumbling block: they refuse to enter God's kingdom themselves, and they hinder others from entering.

Jesus' words expose the lawyers' hypocrisy and their obstruction of the truth. They held the key of knowledge but did not use it to lead people into God's kingdom; instead they became obstacles. Their excessive stress on religious form drove people away from God rather than drawing them near. This passage warns us to take care not to become a stumbling block in the faith, but to help others enter into God's truth and grace.

Through this passage God tells us that he hopes we will faithfully proclaim his truth and help others enter his kingdom. We should use the knowledge God has given us to guide people, not to hinder them. When we are faithful to God's calling, our lives will become a bridge for others to enter God's kingdom.
q: In your life, have you been a help on others' journey of faith, or perhaps unintentionally a hindrance? How can you better use the knowledge God has given you to guide others?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for giving us your word and knowledge. Help us not only to follow you faithfully ourselves but to be a help on others' journey of faith, leading more people into your kingdom. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: As he said these things to them, the scribes and the Pharisees began to be terribly angry, and to draw many things out of him;
lying in wait for him, and seeking to catch him in something he might say, that they might accuse him.
b: This passage records how the Pharisees and lawyers reacted after Jesus rebuked them. They did not repent at his words; instead they grew more hostile and tried to catch him in something he said, so that they could accuse him. These religious leaders were not seeking the truth; they were protecting their own authority and interests.

This passage reminds us that on the path of faith we may meet pressure and challenge from outside. Like the challenges Jesus faced, we too will meet people who twist our words or look for chances to criticize our faith. Yet Jesus' example teaches us that even in such challenges we should hold to the truth and not be shaken by outside pressure.

Through this passage God tells us that even in the face of hostile forces we should hold fast to our faith and stay faithful to God's truth. Our words and conduct should be consistent, and we should be willing to pay a price for the truth. When we remain loyal to God in hardship, we will experience his protection and grace.
q: When you face pressure or criticism from outside, how do you stay faithful to the truth? Today, how can you depend on God more firmly in hard times?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for giving us strength when we face challenges. Help us to hold to our faith and not turn from your truth, whatever pressure we face. May our lives reflect your glory in the midst of challenges. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: Meanwhile, when a multitude of many thousands had gathered together, so much so that they trampled on each other, he began to tell his disciples first of all, “Beware of the yeast of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
But there is nothing covered up that will not be revealed, nor hidden that will not be known.
Therefore whatever you have said in the darkness will be heard in the light. What you have spoken in the ear in the inner rooms will be proclaimed on the housetops.
b: In this passage Jesus gives his disciples an important warning, telling them to beware of the "yeast" of the Pharisees, which is their hypocrisy. Here "yeast" stands for a kind of corruption and falseness that spreads and affects others. Jesus reminds the disciples not to be influenced by conduct that looks pious outwardly but is corrupt within, because in the end everything hidden will be revealed and the truth will come to light.

This passage reminds us that on the path of faith we should keep honesty and purity, consistent inside and out, and avoid every form of hypocrisy. Our words and conduct should match our faith, not only in public but even more in private. Jesus' words stress the importance of transparency and truthfulness, because everything hidden will finally be revealed.

Through this passage God tells us that he expects our faith to be real, shown not only outwardly but flowing from deep within. We should be alert to influences that try to corrupt our spiritual life, and work to live out a true witness of faith in every area of life. When we face ourselves and others honestly, we come closer to God's heart.
q: Is there an area of your life where you need to be more honest with yourself? How can you avoid hypocrisy in daily life and live out a true witness of faith?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for reminding us to beware of hypocrisy. Help us to keep honesty that is consistent inside and out, and not be affected by corruption and falseness. May our faith be purer in your light and become a witness to the world. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: “I tell you, my friends, don’t be afraid of those who kill the body, and after that have no more that they can do.
But I will warn you whom you should fear. Fear him who after he has killed, has power to cast into Gehenna. Yes, I tell you, fear him.
“Aren’t five sparrows sold for two assaria coins? Not one of them is forgotten by God.
But the very hairs of your head are all counted. Therefore don’t be afraid. You are of more value than many sparrows.
b: In this passage Jesus tells his disciples who it is they should truly fear. He warns them not to be afraid of those who can kill the body but can do nothing more, and says the One to fear is God, who holds authority over the soul and our eternal destiny. Jesus goes on to stress God's care for his people: even a tiny sparrow is not forgotten by God, so how much more those he loves?

This passage reminds us that when we face fear and pressure in life, we should turn our eyes to God, the only One we are to fear. The troubles and threats of this world touch only our bodies, but our souls are held in God's hand. He cares about every detail of our lives, even numbering the hairs of our head. Such love should bring us peace and confidence.

Through this passage God tells us that we do not need to fear the threats of this world as long as we remain in his protection and love. Our worth is far greater than anything in this world. God watches over us with boundless love and wisdom, and this should become the source of our strength in every challenge.
q: When you face fear and pressure in life, how do you turn your focus to God and receive strength and peace from him?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for watching over us with boundless love and wisdom. Help us not to fear the threats of this world, but to revere you and trust in your protection and guidance. May we find peace and strength in your love. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: “I tell you, everyone who confesses me before men, the Son of Man will also confess before the angels of God;
but he who denies me in the presence of men will be denied in the presence of God’s angels.
Everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but those who blaspheme against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
When they bring you before the synagogues, the rulers, and the authorities, don’t be anxious how or what you will answer, or what you will say;
for the Holy Spirit will teach you in that same hour what you must say.”
b: In this passage Jesus stresses to his disciples the importance of standing firm in faith. He warns that whoever acknowledges him before others, he will also acknowledge before the angels of God; but whoever denies him before others will be denied as well. Jesus goes on to explain that blasphemy against the Holy Spirit cannot be forgiven, because it involves rejecting and resisting the work and divine nature of God.

This passage reminds us that as Christians we are responsible to acknowledge and witness to Jesus Christ in our lives. When we face challenges or persecution, we should stand firm with courage and trust the Holy Spirit's leading, who will give us wisdom and words at the critical moment. It also reminds us that respect and reverence for God should run through our whole life of faith.

Through this passage God tells us to witness for him with steadfast faith and to trust the Holy Spirit's guidance in our lives. Whatever challenges or difficulties we face, the Spirit of God gives us wisdom and courage so that we can hold fast to our faith and bear a good witness for him.
q: When you face challenges to your faith, how do you steadfastly witness to Jesus Christ? Today, how can you rely more on the Holy Spirit to meet those challenges?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for giving us courage and wisdom to witness for you before the world. Help us, when we face challenges, to rely on the Holy Spirit's guidance and to acknowledge and follow you without wavering. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: One of the multitude said to him, “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.”
But he said to him, “Man, who made me a judge or an arbitrator over you?”
He said to them, “Beware! Keep yourselves from covetousness, for a man’s life doesn’t consist of the abundance of the things which he possesses.”
He spoke a parable to them, saying, “The ground of a certain rich man produced abundantly.
He reasoned within himself, saying, ‘What will I do, because I don’t have room to store my crops?’
He said, ‘This is what I will do. I will pull down my barns, build bigger ones, and there I will store all my grain and my goods.
I will tell my soul, “Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years. Take your ease, eat, drink, and be merry.” ’
“But God said to him, ‘You foolish one, tonight your soul is required of you. The things which you have prepared—whose will they be?’
So is he who lays up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.”
b: In this passage Jesus uses a parable to teach people to be on guard against greed and dependence on wealth. A rich man, whose land produced abundantly, planned to build bigger barns to store more goods, yet never considered how uncertain life is or what God would finally require of him. God's word here reminds us not to center our lives on accumulating possessions, because in the end we cannot take them with us.

This passage reminds us that what is truly valuable is not the wealth we pile up on earth, but being rich toward God. We should think about how to use the resources God has given us to glorify him and bless others, rather than storing up treasure only for ourselves. Our lives are in God's hands, and we must work for eternal values, not temporary material pleasure.

Through this passage God tells us that what he values is our richness before him, not worldly wealth. We should manage the resources God has given us with wisdom, using them for eternal purposes rather than selfishly accumulating riches. Then our lives will be truly full, and we will have his delight.
q: In your life, are you relying too much on material wealth and neglecting God's will? Today, how can you pursue true riches before God?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for reminding us of the true value of life. Help us avoid greed and manage everything you have given us with an eternal perspective. May we be rich not only on earth but before you, and live a full life. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: He said to his disciples, “Therefore I tell you, don’t be anxious for your life, what you will eat, nor yet for your body, what you will wear.
Life is more than food, and the body is more than clothing.
Consider the ravens: they don’t sow, they don’t reap, they have no warehouse or barn, and God feeds them. How much more valuable are you than birds!
Which of you by being anxious can add a cubit to his height?
If then you aren’t able to do even the least things, why are you anxious about the rest?
Consider the lilies, how they grow. They don’t toil, neither do they spin; yet I tell you, even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.
But if this is how God clothes the grass in the field, which today exists, and tomorrow is cast into the oven, how much more will he clothe you, O you of little faith?
Don’t seek what you will eat or what you will drink; neither be anxious.
For the nations of the world seek after all of these things, but your Father knows that you need these things.
But seek God’s Kingdom, and all these things will be added to you.
b: In this passage Jesus urges his disciples not to worry about the basic needs of life. He points to the ravens and the lilies: though they do not labor, God still feeds and clothes them. Jesus reminds the disciples that in God's eyes they are far more valuable than the birds and wildflowers, and God will surely care for their needs. So the disciples should not be anxious about material needs, but focus on seeking God's Kingdom.

This passage reminds us that our lives should not be bound by material needs. Jesus asks us to trust God's provision and to fix our attention on higher things, God's Kingdom and his righteousness. When we focus on these eternal things, God promises to supply our daily needs, so that we can walk the path of faith without anxious looking back.

Through this passage God tells us that his care and provision go far beyond what we imagine. He wants us to stop worrying about daily needs and to focus on seeking his Kingdom. When we depend on God wholeheartedly, he will meet all our needs and give us a fuller life.
q: What things in your life make you anxious? How can you trust God's provision more, and put your focus on seeking his Kingdom?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for providing everything we need in life. Help us no longer to worry about material needs, but to seek your Kingdom and righteousness with all our heart. May our faith be firmer before you, and may we bear witness to your abundant grace. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: Don’t be afraid, little flock, for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the Kingdom.
Sell that which you have, and give gifts to the needy. Make for yourselves purses which don’t grow old, a treasure in the heavens that doesn’t fail, where no thief approaches, neither moth destroys.
For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
b: In this passage Jesus speaks words of comfort and encouragement to his disciples. He calls them a "little flock," showing that in that age they were a small, perhaps feeble-feeling minority. Yet Jesus wants them to know that even though they seem small in number or strength, the Father is pleased to give them the Kingdom. This is a great promise, showing God's love and grace, and it encourages the disciples not to be afraid.

Then Jesus challenges the disciples to sell their possessions, give to the poor, and store up treasure in heaven. This is not merely a literal command, but a call to move their hearts and minds from earthly wealth to heavenly values. Jesus reminds us that true treasure is not on earth but in heaven, an eternal asset that cannot be stolen or destroyed.

Through this passage God tells us that he is pleased to give his Kingdom to those who love and follow him. Our hearts should not be bound by earthly riches but fixed on heavenly treasure, so that our spirits are free to love God and love others, and to live a full life in eternal hope.
q: What is drawing your heart right now? How can you focus more on storing up treasure in heaven rather than wealth on earth?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for giving us an eternal Kingdom. Help us not to be bound by earthly wealth, but to focus on storing up heavenly treasure. May our hearts always turn to you, and find true peace and joy in your love and grace. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: “Let your waist be dressed and your lamps burning.
Be like men watching for their lord, when he returns from the wedding feast; that when he comes and knocks, they may immediately open to him.
Blessed are those servants, whom the lord will find watching when he comes. Most certainly I tell you that he will dress himself, make them recline, and will come and serve them.
They will be blessed if he comes in the second or third watch, and finds them so.
But know this, that if the master of the house had known in what hour the thief was coming, he would have watched, and not allowed his house to be broken into.
Therefore be ready also, for the Son of Man is coming in an hour that you don’t expect him.”
b: In this passage Jesus stresses the importance of staying spiritually alert. Using the parable of servants waiting for their master to return, he tells us to be ready at any time to welcome his coming again. Just as servants must be ready whenever their master comes home, we too should stay alert in faith, constantly preparing our hearts to meet Jesus. His words remind us to be ready not only at certain times or in certain situations, but at every moment.

Jesus' parable goes on to say that whether the master comes in the second watch or the third, the servants found watching are blessed. This teaches us to keep trusting God in every circumstance, and not to let the busyness or difficulties of life lull our hearts to sleep. Jesus compares the watchfulness of a homeowner who knows when a thief is coming to how we should guard our souls, giving no spiritual enemy a chance to break in. Our spiritual life needs constant vigilance, because we do not know when Jesus will return, nor when we will face spiritual challenges.

Through this passage God tells us that spiritual alertness is an indispensable part of the Christian life. We need to be ready at all times, not only to welcome Jesus' return, but also to face the temptations and challenges of life. Only when we stay spiritually awake can we truly act according to God's will and receive his praise when he returns.
q: How do you stay spiritually alert in your life? When you face challenges, how do you make sure you do not stray from God's will?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for reminding us to stay alert and be ready for your coming again. Give us strength to hold fast to our faith and not be distracted by worldly things. May our hearts always turn to you, ready to welcome your coming at any time. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: Peter said to him, “Lord, are you telling this parable to us, or to everybody?”
The Lord said, “Who then is the faithful and wise steward, whom his lord will set over his household, to give them their portion of food at the right times?
Blessed is that servant whom his lord will find doing so when he comes.
Truly I tell you, that he will set him over all that he has.
But if that servant says in his heart, ‘My lord delays his coming,’ and begins to beat the menservants and the maidservants, and to eat and drink, and to be drunken,
then the lord of that servant will come in a day when he isn’t expecting him, and in an hour that he doesn’t know, and will cut him in two, and place his portion with the unfaithful.
That servant, who knew his lord’s will, and didn’t prepare, nor do what he wanted, will be beaten with many stripes,

but he who didn’t know, and did things worthy of stripes, will be beaten with few stripes. To whomever much is given, of him will much be required; and to whom much was entrusted, of him more will be asked.
b: In this passage Peter asks Jesus a question, and Jesus answers with the picture of a faithful and wise steward. Jesus reminds the disciples that as God's servants they have been given an important responsibility: to give the household their food at the proper time. This refers not only to material provision but to spiritual teaching and guidance. His words tell us that if we serve faithfully in the duties God has given, we will receive God's blessing and reward. He wants us to carry out our responsibilities faithfully until he returns, whenever that may be.

But Jesus also warns that if a servant presumes the master will be delayed and begins to indulge himself, that servant will be punished at a time he does not expect. This warning matters greatly for us: we must not grow slack because we think Jesus' return is far off, but keep working faithfully at our posts, because we do not know when the Lord will come back.

Through this passage God tells us that he expects us, as his stewards, to manage faithfully and wisely every responsibility he has entrusted to us. Whether in serving in the church or witnessing in daily life, we must remain faithful. The more grace and responsibility we have received, the greater our accountability, and the higher God's expectations of us.
q: How do you faithfully manage the responsibilities God has entrusted to you in your life and service? Are there any areas that need strengthening so you can be better prepared for the Lord's return?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for giving us spiritual responsibilities and a mission. Help us to be faithful and not slack in them, always ready to welcome your return. Let us live out a witness in daily life and be your faithful and wise stewards. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: “I came to throw fire on the earth. I wish it were already kindled.
But I have a baptism to be baptized with, and how distressed I am until it is accomplished!
Do you think that I have come to give peace in the earth? I tell you, no, but rather division.
For from now on, there will be five in one house divided, three against two, and two against three.

They will be divided, father against son, and son against father; mother against daughter, and daughter against her mother; mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law, and daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.”
b: In this passage Jesus uses very challenging words to reveal to his disciples why he came into the world. The "fire" he speaks of symbolizes the intense reaction his message and teaching would stir up on earth. This fire would bring change and division, because Jesus' message demands a very serious decision. He came not to bring surface peace, but to cause deep change in people's hearts, a change that is often accompanied by conflict with and resistance from the old way of life.

Jesus goes on to say he has a "baptism" yet to be accomplished, pointing to the suffering of the cross he would go through. He eagerly awaited that moment, because it was the key to completing his mission. Jesus understood that his message would cause division within families, because accepting or rejecting him would lead people to different choices of faith, even conflict between the closest of relatives. These words remind us that following Christ means making hard choices, and may even mean facing disagreement with family or friends.

Through this passage God tells us that following Jesus is not an easy road, but a journey full of challenges and choices. We need to be ready for the division and difficulty we may face for the sake of truth and faith. Even so, we must follow the Lord without wavering, because what he gives us is eternal life and true peace.
q: When you face disagreement with family or friends over your faith, how do you keep your faith steady? What specific things can help you keep following the Lord in hard times?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for giving us Jesus Christ. Although the road of following him is full of challenges, give us courage and wisdom to hold to the truth when we face choices and disagreement. May our lives glorify you, and may we faithfully follow Jesus whatever our circumstances. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: He said to the multitudes also, “When you see a cloud rising from the west, immediately you say, ‘A shower is coming,’ and so it happens.
When a south wind blows, you say, ‘There will be a scorching heat,’ and it happens.
You hypocrites! You know how to interpret the appearance of the earth and the sky, but how is it that you don’t interpret this time?
b: In this passage Jesus sharply rebukes the crowd, calling them hypocrites. He points out that they can read the signs of the earth and sky to forecast the weather, yet cannot discern the spiritual time they are living in. Jesus condemns those who seem clever but are blind in spiritual matters. He means that they did not recognize him as the Messiah God had promised, even though his teaching and miracles had made it plain.

Jesus' words remind us that in life we often pay too much attention to the phenomena and changes of the material world, while overlooking spiritual truth and the works of God. This passage calls us not to focus only on present material reality, but to stay sensitive in spirit, to discern what God is doing among us and the spiritual season we are in. This spiritual sensitivity is cultivated through continual prayer, reading Scripture, and drawing near to God.

Through this passage God tells us to observe and discern keenly what God is doing around us, understanding not only changes in the material world but seizing spiritual opportunities and moments. We must avoid being hypocrites and instead live out a true faith, recognizing God's will and submitting to his leading.
q: Are you too focused on the material world and overlooking God's spiritual work? How can you cultivate spiritual sensitivity in daily life and draw closer to God's heart?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for teaching us to be spiritually sensitive. Help us to see not only the changes of the material world but also to discern what you are doing in our lives. Keep our spirits awake, always following your leading, and living out a genuine faith. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: Why don’t you judge for yourselves what is right?

For when you are going with your adversary before the magistrate, try diligently on the way to be released from him, lest perhaps he drag you to the judge, and the judge deliver you to the officer, and the officer throw you into prison.
I tell you, you will by no means get out of there, until you have paid the very last penny.”
b: In this passage Jesus teaches us how to handle relationships and disputes. He calls us to "judge for yourselves what is right," which means facing every situation with wisdom and integrity. Especially when we are in a dispute with someone, we should do our best to settle it privately rather than let the matter grow until it must be resolved through the courts. This teaching stresses the importance of reconciliation and reminds us to avoid unnecessary lawsuits and conflict.

Jesus' words also help us see that when we face problems, we should handle them peacefully rather than let things deteriorate beyond repair. He gives a concrete example: when we have a dispute with someone, we should be reconciled while there is still a chance, or face more serious consequences. This passage reminds us to stay humble, loving, and wise, and to take the initiative in seeking a peaceful resolution.

Through this passage God tells us that reconciliation and forgiveness are indispensable virtues in the Christian life. When we have a disagreement with others, we should seek a solution proactively rather than let the problem fester or worsen. This is not only a protection for ourselves, but also love and respect for others.
q: When there is a dispute in your relationships, are you willing to take the initiative to seek a peaceful solution? How can you let God's wisdom guide you to the right decision in such situations?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for teaching us how to handle conflict and disagreement in relationships. Give us wisdom to resolve differences with peace and love and to live out your teaching. May we choose reconciliation and forgiveness each time we face a challenge, and be witnesses of your love. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.
